findings.affected_surface: Section 1 validity clause and P3b/P4 handling of early termination
findings.claim: The rule leaves non-infra early terminations unaccounted for, allowing outcome-dependent exclusion from the denominators.
findings.evidence: Validity requires five completed turns, but the same clause says the first non-infra attempt is the valid row and capability_fail rows count. Rail exhaustion or scope refusal can terminate work early. No scoring rule resolves this conflict. For example, excluding three early G failures leaves M2_G at 22/27 versus M2_C at 27/30, within the trade margin; counting those failures gives 22/30 versus 27/30, outside it. With the other criteria satisfied, this changes SUCCESS to FAIL-TRADE.
findings.evidence_reference: Section 1, P4 validity and SUCCESS clauses; sections 3.3 and 3.5; section 4, P3b and P4
findings.repair: Freeze treatment of every non-infra early termination: retain every scheduled run ID and either score these outcomes as prespecified capability failures or invalidate the batch. Align this policy with the five-turn requirement and test scope refusal and lineage exhaustion explicitly.

findings.affected_surface: Section 3.5 lineage allocation and persistent identity
findings.claim: The stored counter does not provide the identity binding needed to reject an existing work item presented as a new lineage.
findings.evidence: The adapter allocates a lineage when no lineage ID is passed, yet must reject an existing work item without that ID. The only specified stored record contains lineage_id, budget and retries_used. No persistent work-item-to-lineage binding distinguishes a legitimate first dispatch from the same work redispatched under a fresh run ID, particularly across engines.
findings.evidence_reference: Section 3.5, lineage definition, storage and negative controls
findings.repair: Specify a persistent binding between the existing work-item identity and its lineage. Resolve that binding before allocation, reject missing or mismatched lineage IDs for existing work, and add a negative control that attempts to reset the budget using a fresh run ID or another engine.

findings.affected_surface: Section 0 description of experiment 2
findings.claim: Calling retry text the single changed variable is stronger than the document's own evidence supports.
findings.evidence: Section 0 identifies retry text as the single changed variable. The P1 data paragraph also reports changes to snapshot copying, the analyzer and the batch driver, while section 0 acknowledges that actual invocation flags and loaded settings were not recorded.
findings.evidence_reference: Section 0, experiment 2 and open-anomaly paragraphs; section 4, P1 data paragraph
findings.repair: Describe retry text as the intended treatment change. Separately acknowledge the other harness changes and unrecorded runtime differences, without attributing the cross-batch difference solely to feedback text.

findings.affected_surface: Section 5 interpretation of the third C-only batch
findings.claim: The risk paragraph assigns an interpretation that P1 explicitly says the third baseline cannot establish.
findings.evidence: Section 5 says that a third batch near 11/29 makes the first experiment's C arm the outlier and establishes that experiment 2's comparator stands. P1 repeatedly states that the third batch is reproduction evidence only and excludes no candidate. Reproducing the lower rate does not distinguish sampling from persistent settings, harness or supply differences.
findings.evidence_reference: Section 5, C-arm anomaly risk; KR3; section 4, P1 completion rule and candidates 1 through 5
findings.repair: State that either result adds reproduction evidence while leaving the listed explanations open. Preserve P4's justification through its own concurrent C arm rather than interpreting the third baseline as validating experiment 2.

findings.affected_surface: P2 allowed files and the prohibition on CLAUDE.md and skill edits
findings.claim: The new-script scope conflicts with the repository's mandatory script-inventory convention.
findings.evidence: Repository instructions require a new script to be registered in both CLAUDE.md's scripts inventory and the relevant skill's Available Scripts table. P2 introduces scripts/per-turn-gate.js, but section 2 prohibits both kinds of edits and P2's exact allowed-file list excludes them.
findings.evidence_reference: AGENTS.md, Coding Conventions; plan section 2; section 4, P2; section 6, dispatch boundary
findings.repair: Authorize narrowly bounded inventory-only updates, or explicitly document an exception to the repository convention. Keep behavioral skill and template changes outside scope.

findings.affected_surface: P4 bridge implementation and allowed-file boundaries
findings.claim: The mandatory rail-based evaluation bridge and hash enforcement lack a bounded implementation surface.
findings.evidence: P3 implements the product adapter, and P3b is limited to driver reruns and auth classification. P4 additionally requires routing five-turn evaluations through that adapter, exposing individual verifier checks as Gate commands, and making the analyzer reject hash mismatches. P4 names a fixture but supplies no allowed-file list for these integration changes.
findings.evidence_reference: Section 4, P3, P3b and P4 rows; P4 procedure; section 6, dispatch boundary
findings.repair: Use P4's uncounted bridge run as an explicit preflight implementation step with bounded driver, harness, analyzer and fixture paths. Require a negative control showing that the resume path or a hash mismatch is rejected before freezing counted-run artifacts.

findings.affected_surface: Section 1 KR4; section 3.5 exhaustion order; section 4 P4 procedure
findings.claim: P4 does not isolate the experiment's retry-text contrast: the P3 adapter's post-exhaustion depth-0 repair can fire on G only, so a SUCCESS would promote retry text plus extra G-only repairs the t14 batches never ran.
findings.evidence: KR4 states C is observe-only and G is enforce, and that the sole arm-level difference is whether retry text is dispatched. Section 3.5 step (2) after a round's 2 retries writes gate_exhausted and returns to depth-0, which may dispatch a further repair that reserves the lineage budget. Observe mode records findings and sends nothing, so C never takes that path. Experiment 2 after cap moved on to the next turn inside the eval harness (sections 3.1 and 3.9) with no depth-0 repair. P4 runs both arms through the P3 adapter and treats SUCCESS as promotion of that adapter. The frozen decision rule would then be applied to a G arm that can receive more repairs than C and more than the experiment's per-turn cap.
findings.evidence_reference: Plan section 1 KR4; section 3.5 Order of evaluation steps (1)-(3); section 3.9 Turn versus round; section 4 P4 procedure (both arms through the P3 adapter, no claude -p --resume).
findings.repair: Freeze counted P4 pairs as: on per-round cap, record gate_exhausted and continue to the next t14 turn, matching the eval harness moving on. Do not dispatch depth-0 repairs inside counted pairs. Keep section 3.5 depth-0 repairs for P3 product tests and live lanes. Restate KR4 so the sole arm-level difference is dispatch of the shared formatter retry text; exhaustion is a record and a move-on, and depth-0 repair is out of the counted batch.

findings.affected_surface: Section 3.2 exit mapping; P2 timeout negative control
findings.claim: Timeout handling is contradictory: a 10-second SIGKILL is both a timeout finding and a death-by-signal not_verified outcome.
findings.evidence: Section 3.2 runs each command with /bin/sh -c and a 10-second timeout that sends SIGKILL. A timeout is a finding with evidence timeout. The next sentence classifies death by signal as not_verified, with no retry text and gate exit 2. P2's negative control requires a timeout to be a finding. Classifying the timer's SIGKILL as not_verified would skip retry text and change which items P4 treats as model faults.
findings.evidence_reference: Plan section 3.2 Execution and exit mapping; section 3.8 P2-scope controls (timeout finding with evidence timeout).
findings.repair: Pin the mapping: SIGKILL issued by the gate's 10-second timer is a timeout finding with evidence timeout. Any other signal, including a SIGKILL the gate did not issue, is not_verified and gate exit 2.

findings.affected_surface: Section 3.5 lineage store, reservation, and per-round cap
findings.claim: The lineage budget is not enforceable by the stored counter as written: flock plus rename on the same JSON file drops the lock, a missing directory fail-closes the first retry, and the per-round cap of 2 has no stored field across fresh repair processes.
findings.evidence: Section 3.5 stores {lineage_id, budget: 6, retries_used} at <git-common-dir>/autopilot/gate-lineage/<lineage_id>.json, written under flock -x with an atomic rename. flock is held on an inode; rename replaces that inode, so two processes can both observe retries_used below 6 and both spawn. The store is fail-closed when unwritable: if the directory does not exist, the first allocation exits 2 and KR1 cannot produce a retry. The JSON has no round_id or round_retries_used, while step (2) depends on whether the current round has used its 2 retries and P3 repair processes are fresh. The negative controls require one success when two reservations compete for the last slot, and a crash between reserve and spawn to leave the count spent.
findings.evidence_reference: Plan section 3.5 Storage, Reservation, Order of evaluation, and Negative controls; section 1 KR1.
findings.repair: Flock a sibling lockfile that is never renamed. Create the gate-lineage directory on first use; apply fail-closed only to lock or write failures after that. Persist {lineage_id, budget: 6, retries_used, round_id, round_retries_used} in the same locked update. Set lineage_id equal to the rail run_id of the first gated dispatch and require every redispatch and depth-0 repair to pass that id (P3 already tests a missing id as refused).

findings.affected_surface: Section 4 phases P3, P3b, and P4; KR4 rail-adapter requirement
findings.claim: P4 is not executable as specified: no phase both owns the batch driver and is scoped to run the five-turn t14 loop through the P3 rail adapter.
findings.evidence: P3 allowed files are the section 3.3(A) rail files, the opt-in call, and rail tests; they exclude evals/orchestration/run-t14-gate-batch.js. P3b owns that driver and is scoped to BL-0254 infra reruns, the closed infra_fail list, stop-at-first-non-infra, at most 3 attempts, and mid-run auth_expired. P4 is a pre-registered run that requires both arms on the P3 adapter, a t14 ## Gate fixture, turn n as rail round n, no session resume, an uncounted five-turn bridge demo, and harness/adapter/fixture hashes frozen before the first counted run. P4's negative control marks a G arm that uses session resume, or a C arm that skips the same adapter, as invalid. Leaving the driver on apply_gate plus claude -p --resume makes that control fail on the first pair.
findings.evidence_reference: Plan section 4 table rows P3, P3b, P4; section 1 KR4; section 3.3 candidate A; section 4 P4 procedure paragraph.
findings.repair: Extend P3b (or insert a P3c that must pass before P4) to switch the batch driver onto the P3 adapter: five turns as five rail rounds, ## Gate fixture under the eval task directory, shared formatter, no --resume, BL-0254 reruns preserved, hashes recorded before any counted run. Add a red control that the counted path still calling --resume fails the phase.

findings.affected_surface: Section 3.2 absent ## Gate block
findings.claim: The exit code for flag-on with a caller-requested gate and no ## Gate block is unspecified, so P2 can pass or fail the rail on the same brief.
findings.evidence: Section 3.2 says that if the block is absent, the gate records uncovered: all when a caller asked for a gate and the flag is on, and that with the flag off it does not read the brief (KR2). Exit 0 is pass, exit 1 is findings, exit 2 is malformed or not_verified. Uncovered items are omitted from retry text. A missing block is not called malformed. P2 still has to choose an exit code; exit 2 would stop the round as an operator error, exit 0 would accept and record uncovered.
findings.evidence_reference: Plan section 3.2 Sources (absent block); section 3.2 Execution and exit mapping; section 1 KR2.
findings.repair: Pin this case to exit 0 with uncovered containing all, empty violations and feature_gaps, and no retry. Keep malformed present blocks at exit 2 with no retry.

findings.affected_surface: Section 3.7 Cost versus section 3.5 cap norm
findings.claim: Section 3.7 restates the per-round cap of 2 and the lineage budget of 6, which section 2 and 3.5 forbid other sections from restating.
findings.evidence: Section 2 Caps and the opening of 3.5 say 3.5 is the single normative statement of the per-round cap, the lineage budget, and exhaustion, and that other sections cite it without restating it. Section 3.7 says added model cost is at most 2 extra model rounds per turn or round and a cumulative budget of 6 retries per lineage. A later cap edit in 3.5 can leave 3.7 stale.
findings.evidence_reference: Plan section 2 Caps bullet; section 3.5 first paragraph; section 3.7 first paragraph.
findings.repair: No current change; follow-up only. In a later edit, replace those two numbers in 3.7 with a citation to section 3.5.

findings.affected_surface: Section 0 open-anomaly paragraph and Section 4 P1 candidate 1
findings.claim: The anomaly protocol contains an unresolved evidence-status contradiction: it both says the resolved model IDs were not recorded and states that both raw logs contain one identical ID before P1 checks them.
findings.evidence: Section 0 says the model id actually served was not recorded and is therefore P1 evidence rather than a fact. Candidate 1 then says both rounds' raw logs contain one identical model id, followed by a qualification that P1 must check this before saying so. As written, P1 could mark shared-model evidence as already observed instead of unavailable or unresolved.
findings.evidence_reference: Section 0, paragraph beginning `Open anomaly`; Section 4 P1 candidate (1).
findings.repair: Make candidate 1 explicitly conditional: if the copied logs show one identical resolved model ID in both batches, that observation is consistent with a shared snapshot; if the field is absent or differs, record that result and leave the candidate unresolved. Do not assert that the logs contain the ID before P1 inspects them.

findings.affected_surface: P4 validity clause, run-count procedure, and no-dropping control
findings.claim: The P4 rule is not auditable against selective stopping or omission of favorable pairs because it accepts 27 valid rows without specifying a frozen 30-pair manifest and a terminal disposition for every scheduled pair.
findings.evidence: The validity clause permits 27 through 30 valid runs per arm, while the procedure says not to read outcomes until both arms have their valid-run count or hit an infra ceiling. Neither rule freezes the 30 pair IDs, assignments, order, or a requirement that all 30 IDs reached either a valid row or a recorded infra loss. Consequently, three favorable pairs could be omitted and the remaining 27 could satisfy validity. The negative-control sentence saying not to drop a pair is a prohibition, not an enforcement invariant.
findings.evidence_reference: Section 1 P4 validity clause; Section 4 P4 procedure and negative control.
findings.repair: Before the first counted run, freeze and hash a manifest containing all 30 paired IDs, arm assignment, execution order or randomized seed, and adapter settings. Require every ID to have either one terminal non-infra row or three recorded infra attempts before analysis. Only those declared infra losses may reduce the valid count from 30 to 27 through 29; an omitted, extra, replaced, or post hoc pair invalidates the batch. Add tests for omitting a favorable pair, stopping at 27, and adding a replacement pair.

findings.affected_surface: P4 closed infra_fail classification and P3b rerun driver
findings.claim: The infra_fail set is closed only by labels, not by eligibility predicates, leaving generic runner_error eligible for reruns and making the validity rule gameable.
findings.evidence: The validity clause says infra_fail consists of runner_timeout, runner_error, and auth_expired, but it defines no machine event or source predicate that distinguishes an infrastructure runner_error from a deterministic harness, application, configuration, or product failure. A run can receive two such reruns and then contribute a favorable third attempt. The closed label list therefore does not establish that only infrastructure loss is retried.
findings.evidence_reference: Section 1 P4 validity clause; Section 4 P3b deliverable and acceptance.
findings.repair: Freeze an exhaustive event-to-class mapping in P3b. Define each eligible event from a specific driver signal, including its source and conditions; reserve auth_expired for the verified mid-run OAuth condition. Treat unclassified errors and deterministic child or harness failures as non-infra terminal rows. Add negative tests proving ordinary application errors, bad configuration, assertion failures, and arbitrary runner errors cannot receive a rerun.

findings.affected_surface: Sections 3.5 and 3.9 per-round cap, lineage store, and gate record
findings.claim: The per-round cap has no specified durable atomic counter and is contradicted by an arithmetic statement in section 3.9.
findings.evidence: Section 3.5 stores only lineage_id, budget, and retries_used and explains locking only for the cumulative lineage budget. It never defines the storage identity, reset boundary, or atomic update for the per-round count even though the record is said to carry retries_used for both scopes. A fresh process or concurrent gate pass therefore has no defined authoritative value for the round cap. Section 3.9 then says three dirty rounds can exhaust six retries even if no single round used both retries; one retry in each of three rounds consumes only three.
findings.evidence_reference: Section 3.1 record shape; Section 3.5 storage, reservation, and evaluation order; Section 3.9 turn-versus-round paragraph.
findings.repair: Define an exact round counter schema keyed by lineage and a stable round ID, specify exactly when a new hand commit resets it, and update it under the same fail-closed lock or another named atomic mechanism before dispatch. State whether retries_used is a scalar or an object and give its exact shape. Correct the arithmetic to six one-retry rounds. Add tests for fresh-process reads, reset timing, and three concurrent passes when only one per-round slot remains.

findings.affected_surface: Section 3.2 Gate item grammar and section 3.4 retry formatter
findings.claim: The frozen grammar permits backticks in rule and feature text even though the exact retry format uses those texts inside single backtick code spans and only sanitizes evidence.
findings.evidence: Section 3.2 permits any non-empty single-line text but imposes no backtick restriction. Section 3.4 inserts rule and gap text directly between backticks. Section 3.2 replaces backticks only in evidence. An odd number of backticks in a valid rule or feature therefore produces an unbalanced retry body, while silently escaping or replacing it would violate the frozen experiment-byte formatter contract.
findings.evidence_reference: Section 3.2 Grammar; section 3.2 Execution and exit mapping; section 3.4 Retry message.
findings.repair: Without changing the historical formatter bytes, make a backtick in rule or feature text a malformed Gate item and add parser and formatter negative fixtures for odd and even backtick counts. Alternatively, freeze a byte-preserving escaping rule only if it can be proved compatible with the historical output; rejection is the simpler closed v1 choice.

findings.affected_surface: Allowed-file boundaries for P4, P5, and P6
findings.claim: The phase plan does not bound the repository surfaces for P4 through P6, despite making allowed files a load-bearing phase constraint.
findings.evidence: P2, P3, and P3b enumerate concrete paths. P4 introduces an eval-task fixture, batch header and analyzer artifacts, hashes, and an evidence note without an exhaustive path list. P5 names real lanes and an end-of-pilot report but not its only writable evidence or runtime-state surfaces. P6 names an owner card but no bounded card artifact or report surface. The generic statement that a later dispatch will name allowed files does not provide the frozen phase boundary this plan is meant to specify.
findings.evidence_reference: Section 2 allowed-files constraint; Section 4 rows P4, P5, and P6; Section 6 evidence directory and dispatch boundary.
findings.repair: Enumerate exact allowed repository paths for P4, including the fixture, any analyzer or header changes, tests, and evidence note. For P5, state that runtime dispatch state may append gate records but no product source, brief template, or skill file may change, and name the sole pilot report path. For P6, name the exact decision artifact and forbid source edits. Add a changed-path acceptance control for each phase.

findings.affected_surface: P5 and P6 phase gating
findings.claim: P6 is both potentially reachable without P5 and required to carry a P5 precision table, so the no-promotion terminal path has no executable acceptance.
findings.evidence: The phase order permits P6 after P4 and after P5 only when P5 ran, while P5 may run only after P4 SUCCESS. Thus FAIL-TRADE, no effect, or INCONCLUSIVE reaches P6 without a precision table. The P6 deliverable nevertheless requires one owner card carrying the P4 verdict and the P5 precision table. Section 3.6 also says default consideration waits for P4 and P5 evidence.
findings.evidence_reference: Section 3.6; Section 4 order paragraph and rows P5 and P6.
findings.repair: Split the terminal paths. Make a default-change proposal reachable only after P1 completion, P4 SUCCESS, completed P5, and precision of at least 0.8. For every non-success or no-P5 path, define a separate no-promotion terminal record that carries the actual evidence and cannot approve default-on; do not require a nonexistent P5 table.

findings.claim: The document violates its own single-source rule by repeatedly restating load-bearing caps, attempt limits, and P1 prerequisites, and one repetition is already contradictory.
findings.evidence: Section 3.5 says it is the sole normative cap statement, but section 3.7 repeats two retries and six lineage retries, section 3.9 repeats the cap and makes the three-round arithmetic error, and P3b repeats the three-attempt rule multiple times. The P1 prerequisite is restated in KR3, phase order, phase rows, procedures, risks, and section 6. These repetitions are not merely historical narration and can drift independently during dispatch.
findings.evidence_reference: Section 1 KR3 and P4 validity; Sections 3.5, 3.7, and 3.9; Section 4 order, P3b, P5, and P6 rows; Sections 5 and 6.
findings.repair: Keep each normative rule once in its designated section and replace all other occurrences with stable section references. In particular, centralize the three-attempt validity rule, both retry caps, exhaustion behavior, and the P1-to-P5/P6 prerequisite. Remove duplicated acceptance prose and retain the contradictory arithmetic only after the canonical cap section is corrected.
